teaser: Ten sgit releases turned minutes into seconds; the honest map of what sgit does that Git does not, and where Git is ahead.
core_idea: Between 3 and 27 October sgit shipped ten releases, each fixing a bottleneck a real workload found: a one-file commit on 76,000 files from 29 minutes to 4.6 seconds, a pull on 228,000 files from 566 to 31.7 seconds. The ideas came from earlier work: MGraph-DB's cross-references, Memory-FS's reads by offset, caching on content addresses, and the writer pays. sgit should stop calling itself like Git: Git has no equivalent for encrypted metadata, read keys, blind writes and byte-range folder reads from plain storage; Git also has partial, shallow and no-checkout clones and kept packs; Git is far ahead on merges, identity and ecosystem; one-file reads with no clone and websites from vaults are next.
